best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Energy Regen% boost taking some pressure off your gear when aiming at ER breakpoints. Also upon using Outro, grants the next character switching in a 22.5% ATK boost, amplifying any of your main damage dealers burst windows.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Supportive Echo that can be run at the cost of a sizeable chunk of damage for the character who equips, trading personal gain for team benefits. Should always be used and immediately switch cancelled right before performing an Outro, leading to another DPS. When done so will grant the next character switching in 12% increased DMG% which when combined with the 5P Moonlit set which also grants 22.5% ATK% under the same conditions makes for a sizeable boost. While the echo does lower the damage of whoever wears it, it grants a massive chunk of energy on use usually saving 1 or sometimes even 2 Energy Regen sub stats that may otherwise be needed by the wearer allowing for some damage to be recovered.

best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Havoc DMG% boost alongside adding a large Havoc Damage hit to the Outro of the wearer. Also grants the incoming resonator a Havoc DMG% boost when the wearer uses their Outro. The set is better than Moonlit Clouds if and only if the equipped character's Echoes have endgame investment (with 9 or 10 CRIT substats total) and the character has a 5-star weapon equipped. If both conditions aren't met, Moonlit Clouds is a better choice.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Offers an unconditional 12% Havoc DMG and 12% Basic DMG boost when placed in the Main Echo slot, making it a solid choice for Havoc focused resonators who emphasize Basic damage and are looking to use the 5P Midnight Veil set bonus.

Offers an unconditional 12% Havoc DMG and 12% Heavy Attack DMG boost when placed in the Main Echo slot, making it a solid choice for Havoc focused resonators who emphasize Heavy Attack damage and are looking to use the 5P Midnight Veil set bonus.

best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Havoc DMG% boost and up to an additional 30% Havoc DMG% after you land 4 Basic or Heavy Attacks for a grand total of 40% additional Havoc damage after fully ramped.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: One of the strongest burst damage Echoes in the game that also generates a sizeable chunk of Resonance Energy. What makes this Echo strong is that its damage is delivered in a massive 360 degree area around the target it fixates on and is immediately swap cancellable the second it's used with 0 downsides. When using this Echo, always use it and immediately switch out so it deals it's damage and finishes its animation while the caster of the Echo is off the field. Due to this fact this Echo is normally used outside of characters burst windows.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Changli's signature weapon that's not only fantastic for her but also usable on all damage-focused Sword users who have a large portion of their damage originating from Resonance Skill damage. Offers a huge main stat of CRIT DMG% granting excellent scaling, 12% permanent ATK% and up to 56% increased Resonance Skill DMG% which should be at or close to full power during the bulk of your rotation when opening with one or two resonance skills.

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Danjin is a 4-star Sword Hybrid who buffs Havoc characters through her Outro and deals a good amount of personal damage throughout her rotation. She can accomplish meaningful goals both when doing a fast, buffing-oriented rotation and a longer, DPS-oriented one.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics & Rotation Concepts
paragraphs: Danjin is one of the more complex 4-star characters in the game. That doesn't mean she isn't simple, all 4-stars are, but it does mean she has more combat options than other 4-star characters in the game. This works to her advantage, so it's definitely an upside. Let's establish the important elements one by one before structuring it into coherent rotations.

Danjin's Forte stacks up to 120 points, restored by casting her Resonance Skills, and enables her to cast a Forte Heavy Attack at either 60 or 120 points. This Forte Heavy Attack, called Chaoscleave, instantly restores a ton of Concerto for her (50, being one of the highest Concerto Energy generations from a single move), and can deal great amounts of damage at full power. It also heals 36% of her Max HP on cast.

This attack can be especially strong if followed by the special Basic Attack that combos from it, called Scatterbloom. A fully powered Chaoscleave+Scatterbloom combo is about 2.4x stronger than the half-powered one, but they restore the same amount of Concerto and Resonance Energy. In other words, the half-powered Chaoscleave will be prioritized for Hybrid buffer use (which is how you should be using Danjin meta-wise), while the fully powered one can be utilized as a DPS alongside the Scatterbloom attack if you want to adopt that playstyle.

Her Resonance Skill is also the other key part of her kit. It has no cooldown. When using any Skill, Danjin loses 3% of her Max HP on cast. In practice, this means her Forte Heavy Attack restores more HP than she consumes as a buffer, while as a DPS, she will deplete her HP significantly as her rotation progresses. She has access to 3 different Skill combos, based on what stage of her Basic Attack the Skill is pressed in:

Carmine Gleam: Base Skill, used either after Basic 1 or no Basics, two weak slashes that have the hidden property of comboing into her Basic 2. This is a very useful combo starter when you need a bit more Forte regeneration compared to Basic 1.

Crimson Erosion: After casting Basic 2, Dodge Counter or Intro, Skill can be pressed up to 2 times to perform this combo. Danjin attacks enemies in front with an X-slash. The second hit applies a mark on enemies that lasts for 12s and increases Danjin's DMG Bonus against that target by 20%.

Sanguine Pulse: After casting Basic 3, Skill can be pressed up to 3 times to perform this combo. Danjin chains 3 attacks that restore a large amount of Forte and deal a great amount of damage. Best tool for restoring large amounts of Forte after her mark has been applied on enemies.

Her Outro gives 23% Havoc DMG Amplification to the incoming character for 14s, which expires on swap. This is a relatively small, but still meaningful boost for any Havoc DMG dealer, which enables Danjin to support them. Through her S6, she can also give 20% party-wide ATK when Chaoscleave has been cast.

Finally, while the rest of her passives and Sequence nodes all represent somewhat meaningful damage increases, one of her passives significantly increases her Dodge Counter strength. It now enhances the Crimson Erosion attacks that can follow it up, doubling Forte generation and HP consumption on top of adding 20% DMG Bonus to it. This makes her full Dodge Counter combo restore as much Forte as Sanguine Pulse, which can speed up her rotations against aggressive enemies.

In short, Danjin will always start her rotations with her Intro+Crimson Erosion combo. After that, she needs either 1 or 2 Sanguine Pulse combos to cast her half or full-power Chaoscleave, with or without Scatterbloom to follow up depending on your use case. Her Ultimate intervenes in the middle of her rotation to add some extra damage, and finally she can swap out after that. More complex combos can be crafted, and Dodge Counters can be incorporated, based on your ability to implement Quickswap or the type of enemy you're facing.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
paragraphs: Danjin definitely has one of the most interesting meta histories in the game. From one of the best freely accessible damage dealers to a decent Havoc damage buffer, she's always been one of the reliable 4-star characters, particularly the more of her Sequence nodes get unlocked, in order to increase her damage and buffing capabilities together.

As things currently stand, her main justifiable use case is as a F2P buffer for Phrolova teams. She can buff Phrolova decently and serve as an easy and cheap replacement to Cantarella or Roccia on her team, as she fills a very similar role to them save for their ability to provide extra Echo Skill casts to Phrolova.

However, she still technically can be used as one of the strongest 4-star DPS characters alongside Chixia. While that title is frankly not too impressive, as all 4-stars are honestly very weak as damage dealers, she can get the job done for the lower difficulty endgames, like on Side Tower floors in Tower of Adversity, or even Endstate Matrix if temporary endgame buffs are in her favour. That being said, she is always much better used alongside Phrolova or any other premium Havoc DPS if possible - and as expected of a good 4-star, she is serviceable, but not best in slot in those teams.

In the case of Havoc damage dealers other than Phrollova, like Camellya or Yangyang: Xuanling - overall, other 4-stars exist that buff their respective damage types, being Sanhua and Mortefi, which makes Danjin's lower, but more general buffing potential than those two less appealing. Generally, she's serviceable, but not amazing. And for a basically-free, really old 4-star character? That's fine, and it's unreasonable to expect more from her.

In conclusion, Danjin is one of the better 4-stars in Wuthering Waves. As one of the very few old and free characters that managed to find a somewhat okay meta niche years following her release, she can have her use cases if your account fits the bill. Consider investing in her if you need a free Havoc buffer or an extra, pretty weak but still usable DPS for lower-difficulty endgame content.

synergies.commentary: In Phrolova teams, Danjin is able to fill in nicely for any missing field time as she can adjust between long and short rotations depending on the situation. Besides, via her S6 she is able to give the party a nice ATK buff, she has good personal damage and she's able to amplify Phrolova's Havoc DMG via her Outro, making her one of the best 4-star pairings for Phrolova.

One of Danjin's best Main DPS to support in her Hybrid playstyle. Huge Havoc DMG, the biggest AoE in the game and just a tiny bit of mental illness. Amazing pair despite Danjin falling behind slightly in Camellya teams compared to Roccia and Sanhua.

Easy to play in a hypercarry playstyle, but also usable in a Dual DPS semi-quickswap style, Havoc Rover and Danjin end up very flexible and strong together at all playing levels, all thanks to the general Havoc DMG buff Danjin provides on her Outro (Havoc Rover doing a lot of different DMG types).

Cantarella is the first character to properly enable Danjin to function as a potent Main DPS. She replaces the imperfect alternative of Mortefi, by allowing Danjin to exploit her multiple damage types thanks to her Skill and Havoc DMG Amplify Outro. The two together make for the best 4-star Main DPS team in the game (especially with S6 on Danjin), approaching the strength of some 5-stars (while still performing slightly lower). However, be wary that Danjin's HP loss mechanic is especially accentuated when playing her as a Main DPS, so this team will take a lot of effort to learn.

Roccia is a great option for Main DPS Danjin, sporting solid damage of her own, lots of grouping and a nice 20% Havoc and 25% Basic ATK DMG Amplify on her Outro on top of 200 Flat ATK on her Ultimate, buffs Danjin can make great use of.

The budget option if you want to play Main DPS Danjin and don't have premium 5-stars, amplifying Heavy Attacks (her main type as a Main DPS) by 38%. Providing additional buffs and personal damage with his Sequences, he dishes out some good off-field damage and buffs nicely, which is all Danjin needs. Surprisingly synergistic together thanks to Mortefi's S1 and Danjin's kit allowing him to make great use of his damage potential.

One of the usual Healing Support options that can slot into any team. Super easy to use, provides amazing team-wide ATK% buffs and 15% DMG Amplify with one of the fastest rotations in the game. Enjoy.

Similar to Verina, a premium Healing Support option who can not only slot into any team, but also provide insane 12.5% Crit Rate, 25% Crit DMG, 25% ATK and 15% DMG Amplify buffs to your whole team. One of the best but also easy to use characters in the game.
